messages:
Kai: quick RFC follow-up: proposing a pragmatic 'service anchoring' pattern + tiny 'stitch adapters' to peel off long-lived responsibilities (kv, session-router, prefix-cache) from the runtime. short version: explicit ownership + stable wire shim + iterative cutovers. looking for concerns.

Priya: ok, sketch the failure modes. main worry is added hop causing p95 regression for hotpath.

Kai: agreed. mitigation: two deployment modes. 1) inline adapter (co-located library -> zero extra hop) for hotpath. 2) remote anchor for administrative paths. adapters expose both sync and async ops.

Marcus: how will schema changes be handled? our caches change shape frequently.

Kai: adapters will version payloads. contract includes a 'compatibility level' header. upgrade strategy: minor compatible fields can be ignored; breaking changes require a flagged migration window + dual-read.

Lina: dual-read meaning both runtime and anchor read during window? that's expensive.

Kai: dual-read is for a bounded period only and runs with sampling. plan: sample 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> cutover. plus background reconciliation job to repair divergence.

Priya: what about rollout automation? must be able to rollback quickly if latency or error spike.

Kai: adapters include circuit-breaker + soft-fallback to legacy path. example config snippet: 

```
adapter: {
  mode: "inline|remote",
  fallback: {enabled: true, error_pct: 0.01, latency_ms: 200},
  canary_steps: [1,5,25,100]
}
```

Marcus: metrics: we need anchor_id, adapter_version in traces and a cache-divergence gauge. Also baseline perf numbers so infra can simulate impact.

ArchBot: Created ticket infra#4230 - "service-anchors: perf harness + canary tooling".

Lina: perf baseline idea: run a synthetic load with 95th targeted < 10ms for inline adapters, remote anchors acceptable up to 40ms depending on region. we should codify per-capability SLOs.

Priya: testing: provide a harness that simulates prefix-cache TTLs and session churn. also add DB-stress scenarios for reconciliation.

Kai: will produce a PoC adapter and perf harness. initial timeline: PoC + perf baseline next week, migration runbook draft in two weeks.

Marcus: migration runbook must include key-versioning detail. propose: keys prefixed by v{n}:<original_key> and reconciliation uses tombstone markers for deletions.

Lina: monitoring alert thresholds: 95p latency, extrapolated error-rate jump, divergence_ratio > 0.01. also dashboard with rolling diff sample.

Priya: curious about ownership boundaries. can we standardize anchor surface area to: Read(Get), Write(Put/Update), Observe(Stats), Admin(Drain/Freeze)? keeps shims small.

Kai: yes that's the recommended minimal surface. proto interface: 

```
StitchAdapter {
  get(key): Value | null
  put(key, value, opts): ok
  update(key, patch): ok
  stats(): {hits, misses, divergence_sample}
  admin.freeze(): ok
}
```

Marcus: sounds reasonable. final Q: teams owning anchors need runbook + SLA. who enforces?

Kai: product + infra will maintain an ownership registry. anchors require a runbook and a divergence SLA before accepting production traffic.

ArchBot: Linked docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/anchors/intro and infra ticket 4230. Added watchers: @pri.y, @marcus.m, @lina.

Lina: action items: Kai PoC (next Tue), Priya test harness (next Wed), Marcus runbook sketch (EOW). I'll prepare dashboard templates.

Priya: ack. I'll start with TTL churn scenarios.

Marcus: ack. I'll draft key-versioning and rollback procedures.

Kai: thanks all. i'll write up RFC-followup that includes the minimal contract, canary steps, perf targets, and migration checklist. aiming to keep changes incremental and reversible. :thumbsup:

Lina: +1. incremental wins > giant rewrite. :seedling:
